builds.title: Gold: what is live at /sim today
builds.summary: The published simulator as of the evening of 2026-10-16: new boat model, bucket, depower and brace, drone cam, foam on the back of the wave, welcome card and toolbar, auto quality.
builds.problem: Make the simulator something to show people: one page, clear first minute, runs on a laptop and degrades gracefully on a phone.
implemented: One simulator page with a welcome card, toolbar (help, restart, share, full screen, about), friendly scenario names and an About page.
The v2 boat (V10 Gen 4 hull sections, dry hull has no lift, seat bucket), depower to idle and low brace, segmented trunk, drone camera.
Foam and spray streaks sit on the back of the wave.
Auto quality that follows the frame rate and the drawing-buffer size; phones start light.
review: Open the build, press Start paddling, and paddle for a minute in the default sea.
Switch the camera with V (try Drone), and open the Settings panel to change the scenario.
Tap Down three times, then once more.

questions.text: How smooth does it feel on your laptop (1 = stuttering, 5 = perfectly smooth)?
Did you notice the quality settings changing by themselves, and was a message shown?
What is the first thing that looks wrong?

known: The default desktop settings run at about 20 fps on an M1 Pro until auto quality steps down (item G-009).
The map inset's wave overlay costs 4 to 18 ms per frame (fixed in the next build).
Shilshole land height and sea floor are synthetic; the Gorge walls are procedural; the horizon is procedural.

git.subject: feat: auto quality follows the real frame time and the drawing-buffer size; phones start light; light-effects switch; Low mesh

builds.title: Shoreline 1: real terrain and 14 new places
builds.summary: Land and sea floor now come from public surveys, with a real distant skyline, and the menu gains San Diego, three Hawaii runs, three Gorge runs, Perth (south and north beaches) and Tarifa.
builds.problem: Shilshole land height and sea floor were invented shapes, the Gorge walls were procedural, and only Seattle had a real coastline. A downwind tool should put you on the actual water you would paddle, with the right shore, shoals and horizon.
implemented: A terrain pack per place (`public/sites/<id>/`), built by `scripts/build-site.mjs` from free data: USGS/NOAA CoNED topobathy (Shilshole 12 m, San Diego 15 m), NOAA CUDEM (Maui, Molokai channel, Oahu), USACE Columbia River DEM (Gorge, Rufus), Copernicus GLO-30 plus WA Department of Transport bathymetry (Perth), Copernicus plus EMODnet (Tarifa). Heights are shifted to mean sea level. The depth drives wave shoaling and the shore cut-out, as before.

Shilshole now uses the real survey: the breakwater, the shoals and the bluffs are real. The Ship Canal and Locks appear as water at Sound level: the survey covers the tidal side only, so the canal's pool (about 6 m higher) is not modelled.
A real skyline for each place from the 30 m Copernicus model, with Earth curvature and refraction.
Land colour follows biome (forest, arid, tropical, temperate) and slope, so rock faces show.

14 new scenarios (San Diego 2, Maliko, Kaiwi channel, Oahu south shore, Home Valley, Swell City, Rufus, Perth south 2, Perth north 2, Tarifa poniente and levante). Each has honest notes about what is sourced and what is estimated.
Tests: `test/sites.test.mjs` checks every pack and every scenario (start in water, origin matches, sea fits the shader).
review: Open the build, pick each place from the scenario list, press Space and look around with V (Drone is best).
Shilshole: look at the shore from the water. Do the bluffs, the breakwater and Meadow Point look right? The attribution line at the bottom names the data for each place.
Gorge (real terrain) against the old Gorge scenario: which looks more like the river?
Look at the horizon in each place: is it the right shape and distance?
Does any start put you somewhere wrong (on a reef, too close to land)?

questions.text: Is the real-terrain Gorge better than the procedural one?
How believable is the land at each place (1 = cartoon, 5 = photo)?
Is the Perth north run (Scarborough to Hillarys) one you would paddle? If not, which is?
Which place or run is wrong or missing?

known: Wave height, period and current are estimated from wind and fetch, not measured; the notes say where a number came from. The Perth north run is not a sourced club route. The San Diego run is a paddleboard course used as a stand-in.
Gorge and Rufus: the survey only reaches 1 to 2.5 km from the river, so the upper walls are synthetic, and the river bed is a made-up profile (no bathymetry exists).
Tarifa sea floor is about 100 m resolution; the Moroccan coast is beyond the pack and comes from the skyline.
Fetch is a straight-line estimate, so winding river reaches get less wave growth than a real channel.
The old procedural Gorge scenarios are still in the menu next to the real-terrain ones, for comparison.
Where the survey corridor ends in the Gorge and Rufus (1 to 2.5 km from the river) there is a visible edge where synthetic walls start (G-016).
Tarifa Poniente ends near Punta Carnero; Getares is just outside the terrain. Oahu's course passes south of Diamond Head, so you turn NW to reach Waikiki.
Frame rate on the M1 is not yet measured with a quiet machine; the mesh is not simplified for phones (G-015).
Build size is 26 MB on disk, 18 MB gzipped, against a 25 MB budget that does not say which (G-013 would halve it).
Land is a plain vertex-coloured mesh: no photo drape, buildings, trees or navigation marks yet (G-003 to G-005).

git.subject: feat: attribution per site, tarifa/oahu headings from geometry, skyline outside the pack only and smoothed, gap fill and despike, cache fixes, hardware screenshot tool

builds.title: Map inset rework (G-011)
builds.summary: The map inset's wave overlay is drawn from a patch of sea sized to the waves, refreshed as fast as the eye can tell, at a fraction of the cost.
builds.problem: The overlay sampled the wave field 9,216 times every frame, costing 4 to 18 ms and holding the default desktop settings under budget. A first cheaper version showed false waves (aliasing), went stale when paused and juddered at high zoom.
implemented: Cells are no wider than 1/2.2 of the wavelength below which a quarter of the wave energy lies; the patch is the whole view up to 900 m, otherwise a smaller patch in the middle with feathered edges.

The grid sits on a world lattice, the image is cached and refreshed only as fast as a crest moves 1.2 screen pixels, and refreshed at once when the sea changes (scenario, sliders, crest sharpening) or time runs backwards.
A slow refresh is built across four frames, a fast or abrupt one in a single frame.
Skeptic suite: 7 scenario files (direction of travel, aliasing, judder, staleness, break-it cases, CPU cost, frame rate) all pass.
review: Open the build and let it run (Space). Look at the map in the bottom-right: do the light bands move the way the arrow says the waves go?
Change the map zoom with the mouse wheel over the map, from the whole view in to 60 m.
Pause, switch scenario in the panel: does the map change with it?

questions.text: Do the waves on the map move in the direction you expect?
Is the small patch with soft edges acceptable at the default zoom?
Does the map look better or worse than before (1 = worse, 3 = same, 5 = better)?
Anything odd when you zoom or scrub?

known: At the default zoom the waves fill a 457 m patch (about a third of the map width), not the whole 1.4 km map. This is a taste call: the alternative is a coarser overlay across the whole map that would show false waves.
The Waves and Profile insets still sample every frame (item G-012).
